A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BandRC work. All nine pages of v1 and eleven pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix; both mention supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: v1 reports original BandRC results for spectral-bias experiments, image reconstruction, denoising, super-resolution, inpainting and occupancy reconstruction. Attribution of some occupancy baseline scores to WIRE does not affect the originality of BandRC's results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and additionally reports aggregate Kodak performance, convergence and layer-frequency analyses, and a width/depth ablation.

M1.justification: v1 passes harmonizer outputs directly to activation parameters. v2 inserts sigmoid regularizers that constrain T and zeta within preset bounds (Section 3.1, Equation 4 and Figure 1). This adds a parameter-control step while retaining the raised-cosine activation, complex normalization and prior-conditioning architecture.

E1.justification: Synthetic-chirp representation, Kodak reconstruction, DIV2K restoration, Celtic-knot inpainting and Thai-statue occupancy remain the evaluated coverage. Reporting more Kodak samples and additional network diagnostics does not introduce a new task, domain or population.

E2.justification: v1's displayed Kodak reconstruction comparison includes INCODE, WIRE, SIREN and GAUSS (Figure 5). v2 retains this comparison as Figure 7 and additionally evaluates ReLU+PE in the Kodak aggregate and convergence comparisons (Table 1 and Figure 6). ReLU+PE was already evaluated on other tasks; the established comparator sets remain otherwise intact.

E3.justification: v2 adds explicit 24-image PSNR aggregation, measurements of Fourier spectra across five layers, and convergence traces through 500 epochs. Table 4 introduces a 1000-epoch Kodak-22 evaluation across depths 2–4 and widths 64–512, using depth-dependent learning rates. These substantially expand the evaluation design. Its stated choice of three hidden layers conflicts with the retained four-hidden-layer description, so a changed default for earlier experiments cannot be established.

E4.justification: New Section 3.4 and Figure 5 examine high-frequency representation across individual layers; Figure 6(b) examines convergence; Table 4 tests width/depth sensitivity. These add substantial mechanism and capacity analyses beyond v1's Chebyshev-coefficient and output-spectrum comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's averages across Kodak images and convergence curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds Kodak means of 41.24 dB for BandRC versus 35.57 dB for INCODE, per-image and convergence results, layer spectra, and architectural-ablation results reaching 52.00 dB at width 512/depth 4. Figure 3 also changes coefficient magnitudes and the high-order ordering of raised cosine versus Gaussian. Original benchmark figures and super-resolution/occupancy table values are retained; the new aggregates are not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: v2 adds the mathematical definition of the bounded sigmoid parameter map in Equation 4. The harmonic-expansion equations and Chebyshev-approximation reasoning remain substantively unchanged, with no new theorem, proof or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the illustrated reconstruction advantage of +8.93 dB with an average advantage of +5.67 dB across the image dataset; Section 4.1 retains the original example. Introduction contribution 3 additionally claims specialized regularization. The central activation and spectral-bias claims, and the conclusion, remain stable.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the architectural ablation as evidence of scalability and depth-dependent learning-rate requirements, and motivates a 256-wide, three-hidden-layer configuration as an efficiency/fidelity compromise. It also interprets the new layer spectra as support for high-frequency representation. These are localized additions to otherwise retained interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new ablation's 1000-epoch budget, architecture grid and learning rates, and explains that regularizer bounds must be specified before training. Numerical bound values remain absent. Hardware, PyTorch/Adam usage, pretrained feature extractors and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 29 referenced works and substantively identical related-work discussion. Positioning relative to INCODE's prior conditioning, WIRE and SIREN remains unchanged; citation-page updates do not establish research repositioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract, introduction and method edits, adds Section 3.4 and experimental discussion, and corrects some grammar and parameter terminology. The main section sequence and most existing prose, including related work and the conclusion, remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1 with regularizer blocks, updates Figure 2's parameter labels and Figure 3's plotting format, and adds layer-frequency and Kodak/convergence displays plus aggregate and ablation tables. Retained benchmark displays are relocated and renumbered. These substantially expand the visual presentation while preserving the two-column format.

improvement.justification: The 24-image Kodak summary provides broader documented support than v1's single illustrated reconstruction, while the convergence, layer-frequency and capacity analyses improve empirical scrutiny. These benefits support a limited overall improvement. Unspecified regularizer bounds, conflicting depth descriptions and unexplained changes to Figure 3's coefficients limit reproducibility and confidence; the new regularizer's benefit is not isolated experimentally.
